definitions.explanation: The turn to make a move in a board game or strategy game. Primarily used in shogi, go, chess, and similar turn-based games. Can also refer to the advantage of having the initiative or the right to move.

examples.japanese: {次|つぎ}はあなたの{手番|てばん}です。
{相手|あいて}の{手番|てばん}の{間|あいだ}に{作戦|さくせん}を{考|かんが}えた。
examples.english: I thought about my strategy during my opponent's turn.

examples.japanese: {将棋|しょうぎ}では{先手|せんて}の{手番|てばん}は{有利|ゆうり}だと{言|い}われている。
examples.english: In shogi, it is said that having the first turn is an advantage.

notes:
Composed of {手|て} (hand; move) and {番|ばん} (turn; order). Most commonly used in the context of {将棋|しょうぎ} (Japanese chess) and {囲碁|いご} (go), but also applies to any turn-based game including modern board games and video games.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {手番|てばん}が{来|く}る: for one's turn to come
- {手番|てばん}を{渡|わた}す: to pass one's turn
- {先手|せんて}の{手番|てばん}: the first player's turn
- {手番|てばん}を{無駄|むだ}にする: to waste one's turn

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {番|ばん}: turn — more general; used in everyday contexts ({次|つぎ}は{私|わたし}の{番|ばん})
- {順番|じゅんばん}: order/sequence — refers to the ordering of turns rather than a single turn
- {先手|せんて}: first move/initiative — specifically the right to go first
